system_prompt_style.note: Per-phase prompt templates rendered with state/constraints/history; prompt-building code (agent/*.py) not in the bundle.

env_context_strategy.note: Not a repository harness; no prompt/context-assembly code included in the bundle (only config.py).

context_compaction.note: Figure 1 shows a 'History Summary' block but no history-processing code is in the bundle.

observation_format.note: Observations are numeric metrics returned as text/JSON into prompts; no images or trees.

tool_call_format.note: Plans are emitted as JSON objects naming a tool and parameters; no provider function-calling mentioned.

tool_count.evidence_quote: selecting from a toolkit of seven mutation operators
tool_count.note: Seven operators are the model-selectable tools; analysis utilities are harness-invoked, not model-exposed.

edit_primitive.note: No file-editing surface: the artifact edits sequences, not files; no tool registry in the bundle.

tool_schema_source.note: Tool description source (Appendix C / tools code) not included in the evidence.

protocol_standardization.note: No dependency manifest or source tree contents available to check for protocol clients; README pip list only.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: employs a ReAct-style reasoning loop comprising five phases: THINK, PLAN, ACT, OBSERVE, and REFLECT
loop_primitives.note: Explicit PLAN phase; Algorithm 1 loops over n independent candidate templates and selects the best (multi_attempt). Default n=3 (num_candidates).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: The action planQt = (gt,at,Et,Wt) specifies a goalgt, an ordered sequence ofm actions at
planning_granularity.note: Structured plan object with goal, action queue, expected outcomes, risks.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote:
an LLM-driven autonomous agent framework that enablesin silicoprotein de-
sign through template-based directed mutation
multi_agent_topology.note: One agent with phase-specific prompts; a coordinator orchestrates phases, not separate agents.

delegation_mechanism.note: Single coordinator entry point; no delegation tool described in the paper's toolkit.

human_in_loop.note: A single fire-and-forget API call runs the whole closed loop; no approval step in Algorithm 1.

short_term_state.evidence_quote:
The optimization state at iteration t
is defined as:
St = (st,ξt,t,H t)
short_term_state.note: Typed state tuple with current candidate, satisfaction rate, index, history.

long_term_memory.note: History is initialized empty at the start of each run; no cross-run store in config.py.

state_persistence.note: config.py exposes only output_dir; no resume/checkpoint field in the configuration model.

self_verification.evidence_quote: The LLM analyzes iteration effectiveness and whether to continue optimization.
self_verification.note: REFLECT is same-model review of its own iteration. Harness-run predictors validate constraints but are property evaluators, not tests/linters/judge models.

retry_policy.note: Up to 10 refinement iterations per candidate, plus n=3 independent candidate attempts.

rollback.note: Optimization config has thresholds and stop counters but no revert/undo field; Algorithm 1 keeps the best final candidate rather than rolling back.

termination_condition.note: Loop ends on full constraint satisfaction (test_pass analogue), on the model's continuation flag being false, and at max_iterations=10; max_no_improvement=4 is the stall counter.

cost_controls.note: Per-call token cap in LLMConfig; no caching or router fields in the config model.

timeouts.note: No timeout field anywhere in the shipped configuration model (LLMConfig, OptimizationConfig, BlastConfig, Config).

execution_isolation.note: Imported and run in-process in the local conda environment; external predictors invoked as local scripts/APIs.

filesystem_access.note: Runs as the user with ordinary host permissions; no path allowlist in the config model.

network_policy.note: No network restriction field; the run queries remote databases and an LLM endpoint.

permission_model.note: Planned actions execute automatically; the conservation/threshold guard filters proposed edits but no authorization layer gates tool calls.

tracing.evidence_quote: you will get the designed protein sequence file (`.fasta`), structure file (`.pdb`) and analysis report (`.json`) within the `OUTPUT_DIR` folder
tracing.note: JSON analysis report per run; per-iteration history is kept in state. No OTLP export in the config model.

replayability.evidence_quote: you will get the designed protein sequence file (`.fasta`), structure file (`.pdb`) and analysis report (`.json`) within the `OUTPUT_DIR` folder
replayability.note: Outputs are results only; no replay entry point in README usage or config model.

eval_hooks.note: An evaluation module ships in the repo; the paper's 100-task benchmark is in Appendix G.

guardrails.note: Proposed actions are validated against a protected-position set and a stability threshold before execution (conservation_threshold=0.6, ddg_threshold=2.0 in config.py).

target_domain.note: Scientific-discovery domain; no code, GUI or browser targets.

open_source.note: LICENSE file present and full source published; licence text not shown in the bundle.

model_agnostic.note: OpenAI-compatible base_url (default a local Ollama endpoint) with model configurable; the paper evaluates three different backbones.
